name: High-rise multifamily
summary: Type I concrete (or steel) residential towers, typically 12+ stories, with structured or below-grade parking. Concrete frame, window-wall/curtain-wall enclosure, high-speed elevators, pressurization and fire-pump systems and slow vertical schedules put it roughly 1.4x podium per SF. Evidence is moderate: RSMeans 8-24 story range, RLB city multifamily ranges, Terner (California regression) and Brookings Type-I premiums, Florida HFA high-rise factor and an illustrative developer range; no public elemental budget was found.

typicalSize.method: Typical urban rental tower 15-35 stories; 200-450 units common (judgment; RSMeans 8-24 story model spans 80,750-690,000 SF, e1).

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Gross building SF per unit excluding parking: urban tower units ~800-900 net SF (Census median new rental unit 1,000 SF across all types, e14) at ~75-80% efficiency plus amenity floors; Apers' worked example implies ~64% rentable/gross including back-of-house.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Apers: 140-300+ units/acre; widened for smaller and super-tall sites.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Apers: 0.7-1.2 spaces/unit structured; transit-rich CBDs often 0.25-0.5.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Per-unit = perSF x sfPerPrimaryUnit: mid $410 x 1,150 = ~$470k; low $320 x 1,000 = $320k (Sun Belt concrete tower, lean amenities); high ~$590-600 x 1,350 = ~$800k (gateway-city luxury). Cross-checks: Florida LIHTC high-rise hard-cost factor $338-366k/unit (e11, e12 - affordable caps, near the low end); Apers' 200-unit example ~$594k/unit.

perSF.method: Built up from the podium mid ($290/SF, podium-multifamily.json) plus the Type I increment: Terner +$65-71/SF in 2018 dollars (e8) and Brookings '$75 or more' in 2020 dollars (e9) - roughly $95-120 once those older dollars are brought to 2026 (reasoning only; not used as a value) - giving ~$390-410, with extra structured parking. Consistent with RSMeans 8-24 story $250-700 (midpoint $475, e1), Apers $400-675 (e2) and the upper half of RLB city multifamily ranges (NYC $260-510, Chicago $235-505, SF $420-700; e4-e6). Low end = Sun Belt markets (RLB Miami $195-300 for all multifamily, e7). High = gateway-city towers.

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. general conditions (tower crane, hoists) and OH&P, structured parking at ~0.8 spaces/unit (podium or one below-grade level), elevators, generator, amenity floors and on-site work; perSF is per gross residential/amenity SF (parking area excluded, cost included). Excludes land, soft costs, FF&E, off-sites, impact/tap fees, financing and deep multi-level below-grade parking (optional line item).

qualityTiers.method: RSMeans and Apers ranges span ~1.7-2.8x low-to-high (e1, e2); luxury towers (curtain wall, high ceilings, premium finishes) run well above the standard mid, hence the wider luxury step than for wood-frame types.

systemSplit.method: Derived: garden split (RAND Table 3.4 mapping) re-weighted for a Type I concrete tower - concrete frame 03 ~19.5%, framing 06 reduced to interior wood/blocking (2%), enclosure 07+08 ~13.5% (window wall), elevators 14 4%, fire protection 21 2.5% (fire pump, standpipes), HVAC 23 7% (pressurization, central plant/ventilation), plumbing 22 8%, electrical 26 ~9% (generator, distribution), site 31-33 3%. Verify against a tower GMP.

lineItems.name: Structured parking (podium levels or one below-grade level)

cost.method: Derived: WGI 2024 free-standing median $29,900/space (e13) is the floor; parking integrated in a tower base (transfer structure, ventilation, sprinklers, partial below-grade) ~1.2-2.2x that (2026).

lineItems.name: Additional below-grade parking levels (excavation, shoring, dewatering)

cost.method: Derived: deep below-grade spaces typically 2-4x above-grade structure cost (WGI median $29,900, e13) depending on depth, soils and water (2026 judgment).
Derived: installed gearless traction elevator for 20-35 stops ~ $0.4-0.9M each (2026); ~1 car per 70-90 units.

lineItems.name: Life-safety emergency generator and fire pump

cost.method: Derived: high-rise code requires standby power for elevators/pressurization and a fire pump; 500-1,000 kW diesel set with ATS, enclosure and fire pump (2026 judgment).

lineItems.name: Unitized curtain wall in lieu of window wall (premium)

cost.method: Derived: premium of unitized curtain wall over window wall ~ $25-75 per SF of facade (2026 judgment); facade area ~0.45 SF per GSF for a typical tower.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Derived: lobby, amenity floor, roof deck, co-working, fitness ~ $0.8-2M for ~300 units (2026).

pctOfHard.method: RAND market-rate soft/hard 0.19-0.33 incl. financing (e15) across a mostly low/mid-rise sample; Brookings 20-30% of total (e16). High-rise carries more structural/facade/MEP engineering, longer entitlement and insurance (builder's risk, wrap-up), so mid 0.27; excludes construction interest. | Second pass (2026-10-24, main session): Reduced 5 points: RAND-based, includes developer costs and fees. The engine adds impact & tap fees, the developer fee and construction financing as their own lines (docs/BUDGET_ENGINE.md §5), so this bucket must exclude them.

softCosts.notes: Special inspections, wind-tunnel/peer review and OCIP/CCIP insurance push soft costs up for towers.

design.method: Derived industry norm for complex Type I buildings.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard low $320k x 1.14 ~= $365k; hard high $800k x 1.45 ~= $1.16M; rounded.
